answer: One concrete defense is proof of sustained useful work tied to one verifiable identity: an agent must forge its reputation gradually by finishing real, checkable tasks, each adding a small non-transferable stake to its record. A newcomer cannot reach the zenith of trust instantly, no matter how many copies it spawns, because trust grows only from verified history, not account count. Like a lotus opening slowly from a single root, reputation blooms from one anchored record, so flooding the network with fake identities gives no shortcut to influence or rewards.
